title: Show keyboard state that changes what a keystroke types on the lock screen
head: 0c36e2f9b998
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Non-typing devices contribute lock LED state and can choose the advertised layout
leads.consequence: With a power-button device listed ahead of a Danish typing keyboard, the badge says English (US) and Num Lock off even while the typing keyboard is Danish with Num Lock on. This is conditional on the device states; it is not a claim that every power button has Num Lock off. The existing bar model already excludes power-button, sleep-button, lid-switch, video-bus, and hl-virtual-keyboard and explains that other vendor hotkey blocks and Bluetooth AVRCP endpoints also masquerade as keyboards. Hyprland reports lock states for every keyboard-shaped device, even if the named XKB modifier is absent (then false). Filter to typing devices and deliberately choose a relevant keyboard instead of the first non-virtual entry.
leads.triage: corroborated; Same as Opus A (layout device) and B (Num Lock untyped devices).

leads.summary: A first, default layout generates a permanent error-styled badge
leads.consequence: For the stock non-Latin installer configuration, input.lua prepends us to make us,ru; when the lock wrapper resets the layout to index 0, the model still returns English (US), which the view renders as a warning. The manual instead promises a badge for a second layout and an unchanged screen when nothing changes the keys. Compare active_layout_index with zero, and retain the other layout's description only on a non-default index (or describe the different always-on behaviour explicitly).

leads.summary: Failed-to-start hyprctl leaves last badge state stale despite the quiet-state promise
leads.consequence: If a previously successful poll lit Caps Lock and hyprctl becomes absent/unexecutable during an existing lock, Quickshell FailedToStart does not finish the stdout stream. applyKeyboardState is never called to clear the old state; every 400ms a new attempt emits a warning. By contrast a process which starts and exits with empty stdout reaches streamFinished, clearing even a real warning. Handle start error and nonzero exit explicitly, retaining an identified last-good state or marking unknown rather than silently claiming a fresh quiet state; back off repeated failures.
leads.triage: dropped; hyprctl failing to start mid-lock is unrealistic on a Hyprland session; low value.

leads.summary: Named keyboard override can make physical modifier badges disagree with logical modifiers
leads.consequence: The manual recommends altwin:swap_alt_win to make physical Alt act as Super, but modifierForKey classifies native code 64 as Alt irrespective of the remapping; if Qt sends that event with MetaModifier, trackModifiers displays ALT until the next ordinary key resynchronizes from event.modifiers. The symmetric physical Super acting as Alt is similarly mislabeled. Prefer logical modifier state for Ctrl/Alt/Meta or track the key by physical code only for the exceptional Shift release. The shipped XKB symbol definitions map physical Alt to Super/Mod4 and physical Super to Alt/Mod1; Qt Wayland sends the xkb keycode and logical modifier-derived Qt key to the KeyEvent. Prefer logical modifier state for Ctrl/Alt/Meta or track the key by physical code only for the exceptional Shift release.
leads.triage: corroborated_not_published; Opus noted the altwin/ctrl remap mislabels as cosmetic; left out of public comment.

leads.summary: #11858 and #7806 each conflict with this PR's Keys.onPressed hunk
leads.consequence: Own-parent three-way merges of this PR with unstacked #11858 and #7806 each yield conflict markers in Keys.onPressed. Choosing only #11858's side drops press-time modifier tracking, choosing only this PR's side reintroduces typed wake keys. Choosing only #7806's side also drops press-time tracking; choosing only this PR's side restores its auto-repeat password flood. Preserve this PR's modifier call and #11858's wake-key clear/accept plus #7806's early repeat guard if merged, retaining the release handler. GitHub reports both other PRs individually MERGEABLE against their bases, not against this PR.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #7806 and #11858 edit the same Keys.onPressed lines (coord/pr-7806.diff); Opus merge simulation confirmed one text conflict. Mentioned in Details.

leads.summary: Background poll continues on a DPMS-blanked lock even when no keyboard state changes
leads.consequence: The timer launches up to 2.5 hyprctl processes per second for the full locked duration, 9,000 per hour and 72,000 over an eight-hour overnight lock, even with displays blank and no preview. There is no DPMS guard, in contrast to the existing video-only 3-second monitor poll. Consider a slower steady-state poll or event-assisted refresh/backoff, especially after blanking, preserving initial and keyboard-triggered reads.

leads.summary: New tests still pass when the service drops every hyprctl response
leads.consequence: The Node test only regex-checks that the process and timer exist, while the QML badge fixture injects state directly into LockView; neither verifies that Process stdout is consumed. Replacing Service's onStreamFinished handler with an empty block made the complete new Node test pass, yet live badges would remain at their initial quiet state. Add a service-level integration check or an assertion that wires the collector to applyKeyboardState and the lock view (a regex alone remains weaker than runtime coverage).
leads.triage: corroborated_partially; Same class as the Opus surviving mutants; public note cites Opus's three mutants only. The collector mutant is Sol-only evidence and not published.

leads.summary: #10130 and this PR conflict on the lock status JSON fields
leads.consequence: Unstacked #10130 adds blankArmed and activityIdle to status() at exactly the insertion point where this PR adds keyboard. A merge against #10130's own parent yields conflict markers. Both sides' fields are independent, so a resolver must include all three; choosing only the keyboard side drops #10130's new diagnostics, choosing the other side drops this PR's status keyboard information. #10130 is MERGEABLE against its own base, not necessarily this PR.
leads.triage: verified_by_coordinator; #10130 adds status() fields at the same insertion point (coord/pr-10130.diff); Opus merge simulation confirmed. Mentioned in Details.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With two or more layouts configured, Super + Ctrl + L, idle and lid-close locks show a red badge for the default layout.

### Layout badge shows for the default layout

`keyboardStateFromDevices` names `active_keymap` whenever `layout` contains a comma. `omarchy-system-lock` switches every keyboard to layout 0 as it locks, so `us,dk` and the `us,<layout>` default for non-Latin installs get `ENGLISH (US)` on each such lock. It also reads the first listed device, which can be a power button that Left Alt + Right Alt does not switch, so a switch made at the lock is not shown.

**Suggested change:** Name a keyboard's layout only when its `active_layout_index` is above 0.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 0c36e2f)</summary>

Save as `test/shell.d/lock-keyboard-state-default-layout-test.sh` (same helpers and style as the PR's `lock-keyboard-state-model-test.sh`) and run `bash test/shell.d/lock-keyboard-state-default-layout-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const model = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/lock/KeyboardStateModel.js')

function devices(keyboards) {
  return JSON.stringify({ mice: [], keyboards: keyboards })
}

// Two layouts configured (the manual's "us,dk" example, or the "us,<layout>"
// that default/hypr/input.lua writes for a non-Latin install), and the keyboard
// on the first one: omarchy-system-lock runs `hyprctl switchxkblayout all 0`
// before the lock screen shows, so this is the state at the start of every lock.
assertDeepEqual(
  model.keyboardStateFromDevices(devices([
    { name: 'keychron', layout: 'us,dk', active_layout_index: 0, active_keymap: 'English (US)', capsLock: false, numLock: true, main: true }
  ])),
  { capsLockOn: false, numLockOn: true, layoutLabel: '' },
  'the first (default) layout of a multi-layout config shows no layout badge'
)
JS
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (stdout empty, exit status 1):

```
expected: {"capsLockOn":false,"numLockOn":true,"layoutLabel":""}
actual:   {"capsLockOn":false,"numLockOn":true,"layoutLabel":"English (US)"}
not ok - the first (default) layout of a multi-layout config shows no layout badge
```

`LockView.qml` turns a non-empty `layoutLabel` into an `ENGLISH (US)` badge with `warn: true` (the `border-error` / `text-error` colours).

Run with Node v26.7.0. The same test passes against a copy of the model that only names the layout when `active_layout_index` is above 0.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

#### Keyboard poll keeps running while the lock is blanked

The 400 ms `hyprctl devices -j` timer keeps running while the displays are blanked (9,000 launches an hour), when no badge is visible. Found in source; not measured on a real lock.

**Suggested change:** `running: (root.locked && !root.displaysBlank) || root.previewVisible`, updating the `running:` regex in the model test.

#### NUM LOCK OFF can stay lit (only with `numlock_by_default = false`)

Devices nobody types on (for example the power button) count as keyboards, and Hyprland keeps Num Lock per keyboard. Turning Num Lock on at the keyboard then leaves the badge lit for the whole lock.

**Suggested change:** Skip the devices `KeyboardLayoutModel.js` already treats as untyped (`isTypedKeyboard`) before reading any state.

Applies when `numlock_by_default = false` is set in `~/.config/hypr/input.lua` (Omarchy's default is `true`). Hyprland keeps Num Lock per keyboard (`m_modifiersState.locked`), so pressing Num Lock turns it on only for the keyboard it was pressed on.

Save as `test/shell.d/lock-keyboard-state-typed-numlock-test.sh` and run `bash test/shell.d/lock-keyboard-state-typed-numlock-test.sh` from the repository root.

```bash
#!/bin/bash

set -euo pipefail

source "$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)/base-test.sh"

run_node_test <<'JS'
const model = requireFromRoot('shell/plugins/lock/KeyboardStateModel.js')

function devices(keyboards) {
  return JSON.stringify({ mice: [], keyboards: keyboards })
}

// numlock_by_default = false in ~/.config/hypr/input.lua: every keyboard starts
// with Num Lock off. Pressing Num Lock turns it on for the keyboard it was
// pressed on only; the power button, which nobody presses Num Lock on, keeps it
// off for the rest of the session.
assertDeepEqual(
  model.keyboardStateFromDevices(devices([
    { name: 'power-button', layout: 'us', active_layout_index: 0, active_keymap: 'English (US)', capsLock: false, numLock: false, main: false },
    { name: 'at-translated-set-2-keyboard', layout: 'us', active_layout_index: 0, active_keymap: 'English (US)', capsLock: false, numLock: true, main: true }
  ])),
  { capsLockOn: false, numLockOn: true, layoutLabel: '' },
  'Num Lock turned on at the keyboard clears NUM LOCK OFF'
)
JS
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (stdout empty, exit status 1):

```
expected: {"capsLockOn":false,"numLockOn":true,"layoutLabel":""}
actual:   {"capsLockOn":false,"numLockOn":false,"layoutLabel":""}
not ok - Num Lock turned on at the keyboard clears NUM LOCK OFF
```

Run with Node v26.7.0. The same test passes against a copy of the model that skips the device names the bar's `UNTYPED_KEYBOARDS` pattern (in `KeyboardLayoutModel.js`) matches.

#### AltGr shows the ALT warning

Keycode 108 (Right Alt) maps to `Qt.AltModifier`, but on dk, de, fr, pl and most other non-US layouts it is AltGr, used to type password characters (such as `@` on dk, de, fr). Holding it shows a red `ALT` badge until the next character.

**Suggested change:** For keycode 108, return 0 when `event.key === Qt.Key_AltGr`.

On layouts that include `level3(ralt_switch)` (dk, de, fr, pl and most non-US layouts), Right Alt is AltGr: xkb keycode 108, keysym `ISO_Level3_Shift`, which Qt reports as `Qt.Key_AltGr` with no Alt modifier. `modifierForKey` maps keycode 108 to `Qt.AltModifier`, so holding AltGr to type a password character such as `@` shows a red `ALT` badge. The next character key clears it, because its `event.modifiers` carries no Alt.

The quickest form is two lines added to the PR's own fixture, `test/shell.d/fixtures/lock-keyboard-state/shell.qml`, right after the Super checks:

```qml
view.trackModifiers(keyEvent(Qt.Key_AltGr, 108, 0), true)
root.assertTrue(labels(view).indexOf("ALT") === -1, "holding AltGr raises no ALT warning, got " + labels(view))
```

The run below used the same check in a standalone fixture: a copy of the PR's `lock-keyboard-state/shell.qml` whose test body is replaced by these steps, plus a copy of `lock-keyboard-state-badges-test.sh` pointed at it. An excerpt of the fixture's timer handler:

```qml
        var view = component.createObject(host, { width: 800, height: 600, loadBackground: false })
        if (!view) {
          root.fail("LockView failed to instantiate: " + component.errorString())
          return
        }

        // On layouts that put ISO_Level3_Shift on Right Alt (dk, de, fr, pl
        // and most others), Right Alt is AltGr: xkb keycode 108, reported by
        // Qt as Key_AltGr with no Alt modifier. Holding it to type a password
        // character such as @ or { is ordinary typing.
        view.trackModifiers(keyEvent(Qt.Key_AltGr, 108, 0), true)
        root.assertTrue(labels(view).indexOf("ALT") === -1,
          "holding AltGr raises no ALT warning, got " + labels(view))

        view.destroy()
```

Actual output at the reviewed head (stdout empty, exit status 1). No compositor was available, so the test's `require_compositor` line was bypassed and Quickshell ran with `QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen` (the fixture creates no window). The five Quickshell log lines between `Lock keyboard state log:` and `not ok` are omitted here because they only give sandbox paths and IDs:

```
Lock keyboard state result:
{
  "ok": false,
  "failures": [
    "holding AltGr raises no ALT warning, got ALT"
  ]
}
Lock keyboard state log:
not ok - AltGr, which types characters, is not reported as ALT
```

In the same run, and under the same offscreen setup, the PR's own `lock-keyboard-state-badges-test.sh` passed at the head, and the existing `lock-fingerprint-indicator` and `lock-password-overflow` tests passed too.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified**
- Both new tests pass at the head and fail at the merge-base.
- A Shift release reported as `Qt.Key_CapsLock` under `shift:both_capslock_cancel` clears the SHIFT badge (keycode path).
- With nothing to report, the badge row is hidden and the field layout is unchanged.
- A failing `hyprctl` (error text on stdout) yields the quiet state.

**Optional test improvement:** With the tests unchanged, each of these edits still leaves both new tests passing: removing `Keys.onReleased`, removing the `onActiveFocusChanged` reset, or removing `onKeyboardActivity: root.refreshKeyboardState()`. The QML fixture sets view properties and calls `trackModifiers()` directly, so the key handlers and the key-triggered refresh are untested.

**Related open PRs:** #11858 and #7806 change the same `Keys.onPressed` lines in `LockView.qml`, and #10130 adds fields at the same place in `Service.qml`'s `status()`. These are text conflicts in which both sides should be kept.
</details>
